Use the first print rounded to one decimal place; ignore later CPS ASEC, SPM-methodology, or table revisions unless the original release is formally corrected before the same release day ends.","dataPointId":"census.cps_asec.spm.child_under18_poverty_rate.2027.first_print","historicalContext":[{"label":"2024 first print child SPM poverty rate","value":13.8},{"label":"2023 first print child SPM poverty rate","value":13.7},{"label":"2022 first print child SPM poverty rate","value":12.4},{"label":"2021 first print child SPM poverty rate","value":5.2},{"label":"2019 pre-pandemic child SPM poverty rate","value":12.6}],"drivers":["SPM includes taxes, refundable credits, noncash transfers, medical expenses, work expenses, and geographic housing-cost adjustments","recent post-pandemic child SPM rates have re-centered near 13 to 14 percent after the temporary 2021 child tax credit expansion expired","calendar-year 2027 rate is sensitive to refundable tax-credit law, SNAP and school-meal policy, child-care and medical out-of-pocket costs, and labor-market income","first-print CPS ASEC sampling and processing noise warrants a wide interval even without a structural policy shift"],"sourceContext":["https://www.census.gov/library/publications/2025/demo/p60-287.html","https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/demo/tables/p60/287/tableB-2.xlsx","https://www.census.gov/library/publications/2024/demo/p60-283.html","https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/demo/tables/p60/283/tableB-2.xlsx","https://www.census.gov/newsroom/releases/calendar.html"],"runAt":"2026-06-27T14:15:49Z","reasoning":[{"kind":"heading","text":"Forecast for calendar-year 2027 child Supplemental Poverty Measure poverty rate"},{"kind":"text","text":"The resolver is the Census Bureau's first published SPM poverty rate for people under age 18 for calendar year 2027.
